composition.mass: Visual weight forms an upright triangular wedge in the upper centre, anchored by the elevated head and ears and tapering down to the narrow approach at row 10.
composition.read: The viewer's eye enters through the narrow canvas-stone approach at the south rim, drawn northward along the bright yellow paint-band path. Flanking bristle clusters and pigment pots guide attention up the stepped tiers to the vocalising feline bust. The stark surrounding void reproduces the unpainted raw cotton canvas perimeter framing the original acrylic painting.

lighting.notes: studio high-key glare across unpainted primed canvas: Follows the value structure where 40% of the field is bare primed white cotton canvas radiating an even, shadowless studio wash.

rules: Keep all outer boundary cells as void to mimic unpainted studio canvas margins.
Ensure the raised tiers are concentrated behind and beneath the central feline bust.
Concentrate cadmium yellow sand exclusively along the central path axis.
Cluster bristle tufts along transitions between raised cliff faces and lower ground.

lens.aspect: material and marks: acrylic impasto slabs, bristle drags, dry-brush scumbles, and raw exposed canvas
lens.summary: A stepped island formed like a heavy wedge of dried acrylic paint paste floating in an empty field of primed cotton canvas.
lens.differs: Unlike architectural or landscape readings, every landmass is treated as a physical swatch of thick unblended paint, with cliffs formed by knife cutaways and the background left as stark, unpainted primed canvas weave.

shaper.name: patchwork
shaper.why: IMAGE 1 is composed of flat, unblended fauvist swatches of opaque acrylic applied with directional brushwork, directly translated into rectangular block patches of saturated colour stepping in height.

surface_mix.why: Fiery orange dirt and cadmium yellow sand represent the dominant acrylic strokes of the chest and bib, while stone models raw canvas patches and grass gives the singular viridian neck accent.

cliff_treatment.why: Upper cliffs carry the deep ultramarine-indigo of the brow and ears, while lower cliffs carry the deep magenta-crimson of the left chest.

concept.name: lens-medium
concept.fragment: LENS "medium": the artwork's MATERIAL AND MARKS become the island's physical character. Start from ANALYSIS.medium and ANALYSIS.palette, not from the subject. The ground is made of the marks: single-stroke ink becomes ribbon land and sweeping arcs of path with void where the paper is empty (shaper "ribbon", or "spiral" for a curl); airbrush gradients become soft radial terraces fading outward (shaper "radial"); fauvist or knife strokes become a patchwork of flat colour blocks at different heights (shaper "patchwork"); charcoal smudge becomes soft-edged dark masses with pale mist lying in the hollows (shaper "mound" or "basin"); pencil hatching or scratchy ink becomes angular slabs split by thin seams (shaper "shards"); vector doodles become dense small ornament on a tidy mirrored plan (shaper "symmetric"). Choose shaper params from the marks themselves (how many strokes, how wide, which way they sweep, how many blocks). Palette, surface_mix and cliff_treatment follow the medium (ink: paper-pale sand and ink-dark cliffs; airbrush: rings of surfaces fading by value; fauvist: saturated patches; charcoal: soft grey-green, mossy or soft cliffs). New props are the marks made solid: a brush flick as a curved blade of stone, a smudge as a low soft boulder, a doodle as a ring of beads, a knife stroke as a flat tilted slab. The figure's pose comes from how it is drawn (a single continuous stroke, a stack of colour patches), and it may be a monument of the marks rather than a living creature.
